summary.headline: Aditya Infotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 89.5% YoY to INR1,402 crore; EBITDA margin 14.8%, adjusted PAT INR142.2 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue of INR1,402 crore grew 89.5% YoY, with CP PLUS contributing about 87% of revenue and IP products about 79% of the CP PLUS portfolio. EBITDA rose 20% YoY to INR208 crore, with margin up 604 bps to 14.8%, helped by product and brand mix and operating efficiencies. Gross margin was 30.8%, up 8-10 bps YoY but moderated from Q4 as lower-cost inventory was exhausted. Adjusted PAT of INR142.2 crore rose 332.5% YoY, aided by a 59% fall in finance costs; management reiterated its FY27 EBITDA guidance of 14-15%.

segments.name: CP PLUS (brand)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 87% of Q1 revenue; IP products were about 79% of the CP PLUS portfolio, reflecting shift to higher-value AI surveillance.

segments.name: Nexivue (second brand)
segments.commentary: Rollout being accelerated in coming months with a wider portfolio to extend channel coverage; no revenue disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 14-15% reiterated; Q1 at 14.8%; management will stick to guidance and revisit after H1 results.
FY27 revenue guidance cited by an analyst as INR60-65 billion; management did not dispute it on the call.
Price increases of 10-20% taken so far by product; expected 15-20% cumulative by end of H1 and about 25% for FY27 overall.
Backward-integration plants (housing and enclosures) operational by Q3 FY27; in-house scale manufacturing to kick off in Q3-Q4 FY27.
CP PLUS Pro series and Home IoT products targeted to go live by end-Q3/beginning-Q4 FY27; exports expected to be significant in 18-24 months.
Corelink Cable JV (with Orient Cables) to start commercial production by end of FY27.
capex_capacity: Current capacity about 2.5 million units per month at Kadapa; utilisation about 85-90%.
Plan to roughly double capacity in the next three years via Kadapa expansion (land acquisition in final stages) and a second cluster in Greater Noida (land identified, allocation applied).
Adding three FA lines and one MI line in August; total 42 FA, 4 MI and 12 SMT lines by end-August.
Corelink Cable JV plant in Rajasthan of about 1 lakh sq ft, expected commercial production by end of FY27.
New corporate office and R&D centre inaugurated 2 August 2026; three R&D centres operating (Noida, Ahmedabad, Taiwan), Bengaluru opening shortly.
Lens backward-integration: trial automatic line being set up; fully automated plant planned.
demand_pricing: Market share 43.3% in Indian video surveillance in FY26 (Frost & Sullivan), roughly doubled over the period shown.
Price hikes of 10-20% by product, taken monthly, bi-monthly or quarterly, to pass through DDR and SOC cost inflation; management says no major consumption impact seen so far.
STQC norms bar Chinese semiconductors and memory; about 40+ brands now certified, so competition is rising, though management says scale helps it secure components.
Management is moving to top-down demand generation targeting enterprise, government and AI projects through SIs and channel.
Imported BOM: about 35% from Taiwan (semiconductors), 15-20% passives (Taiwan and China); current mix about 55-60% imported and 40% domestic, targeted over the next two quarters.
No impact from the Middle East crisis on supply chain so far; some forex impact noted, which is hedged.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes were taken this quarter, and is there a gap between current market prices and inventory cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Hikes ranged 10-20% by product, passed gradually to avoid a shock to consumers; management expects to keep passing costs through in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What margin improvement can be expected from backward integration in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify; said housing, enclosures, cable connectors, lenses and later bare PCBs add basis points, and semiconductors and passives will not be localised.

qa_highlights.question: Can new categories add INR5,000-10,000 crore of TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to size; Pro series addresses global-brand share, home IoT is a new market, and industrial automation and drone gimbal cameras are at study stage.

qa_highlights.question: Is there further margin upside beyond 14-15% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it stands by the 14-15% guidance, aims to beat it internally, and will comment after H1 results.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the BOM is imported?
qa_highlights.answer: About 55-60% imported (35% Taiwan semiconductors, 15-20% passives) and 40% domestic, targeted over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is forex managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging policy keeps cover between 85% and 100% of receivables and payables, currently about 90%, with weekly hedging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity and utilisation, and what is the capex timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: 2.5 million units per month at 85-90% utilisation; capacity to roughly double in three years, with gradual quarterly ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the average price increase so far and the remaining need?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15-20% average by end-H1 and around 25% for the full year, reviewed monthly and quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How secure is chip sourcing and what changed in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: SOC and memory are covered for three to four quarters via rolling forecasts; other expenses rise is in line with seasonality (marketing at 30-32% of annual spend in Q1) and inflation.

risks_watch: Component cost inflation in DDR and SOC; pass-through lag could compress margins if price hikes slow.
Gross margin moderated QoQ as low-cost inventory was exhausted; watch for further compression in Q2.
Competition from 40+ STQC-certified brands; watch market share versus the 43.3% FY26 base.
Export ramp is 18-24 months out and new categories are at early stage; revenue impact is uncertain.
Forex: about 10% of exposure is unhedged; management says the forex impact was small so far.
Management is evasive on TAM sizing and margin upside, and declined to give specific figures.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margin and balance-sheet delivery, but cautious and non-committal on forward numbers: it held to 14-15% EBITDA guidance, declined to quantify TAM, backward-integration margin gains and R&D spend, and gave timelines only in broad terms.

financial_highlights.change: Improved; inventory and debtor days lower

key_quotes: So, we are trying to not pass the whole by price hike at one go in the market because the cost hike in DDR and SOC has been phenomenal across all product categories and not only CCTV.

So, I would probably not be able to comment exactly what percentage of margin improvement will happen but yes there will be couple of basis points in the coming future as we scale up each aspect of the localization.

We in quarter one stand by that only, I think we are at 14.8%. We , at this moment would stick to the guidance and internally we always try to beat the guidance but I think we will probably comment more on that after the half year results.
So, all our supply chain is from Taiwan and that's almost 35% of the BOM. Another 15%, 20% is passive electronics.
So, we have broadly spoken about almost doubling this capacity in the next three years.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR60-65 billion (cited by analyst, not disputed) implies roughly 62.5% growth at midpoint on Q1-led run-rate context, backed by near-full utilisation (85-90%) and a planned near-doubling of capacity over three years, though the 62.5% figure is derived from the brief's guidance range rather than a stated base year, so treat it as indicative.
